rows.Origin: Bred by Mark C. Spies (United States, 1981).
rows.Bloom: Pink. Mild fragrance. 60 petals. Average diameter 1.5". Double (17-25 petals) bloom form. Prolific, continuous (perpetual) bloom throughout the season.
rows.Growing: USDA zone 5b through 10b. Disease susceptibility: disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) . Can be grown in the ground or in a container (container requires winter protection).
